title: Big election winners
primary_topics: Big-election-winners tribute column June 2, 2013 -- fourth of automated-elections quadrilogy (E100 → A458 → B19 → E99)

Public-school-teachers-as-PCOS-winners thesis: Comelec 'always deputizes' them to administer polls at precinct level; PCOS spared them from 'harrowing physical work, nighttime terror threats and tedious legal hassles' -- three-prong relief

No-manual-tallying section: under old system teachers remained at polling places into 'wee hours of the following morning' to count manually handwritten entries + enter in 'taras' on tally boards and score sheets

Manual-counting nightmares: illegible entries / two-different-hands-invalid-ballots / candidates' names written on wrong spaces (mayor on vice-mayor spaces) / extraneous writings or strange drawings → 'marked ballots' used by bribers to verify 'victims' votes; lawyer 'objections' confounded teachers and 'interminably delayed the count'

Automation eliminates: machine-tally instant + electronic transmission to municipal/city BOCs; teachers freed from physically carrying election documents and ballot boxes from remote polling places to town centers 'in the dead of night'

Parenthetical caveat: 'I am not unmindful of the fact that due to transmission glitches in many -- as many as 18,000 of the 78,000 -- PCOS machines, several teachers unfortunately had to bring the compact flash cards and/or the machines themselves to the election centers'

No-legal-hassles section: 'PCOS count at precinct level happened faster than the speed of knowledge' (signature aesthetic phrase); old technical delays obsolete; teachers no longer manually preparing election returns + signing/sealing/packing/locking inside ballot boxes; 'could no longer be blamed and sued by nosy lawyers and desperate candidates looking for scapegoats for their defeat'; no more preproclamation controversies -- 'scourge of teachers because they were often bribed or threatened or forced to falsify election returns'

Other-winners section: Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting (PPCRV) led by Ambassador Tita de Villa -- 'volunteer army of 350,000'; parallel-counts (electronic + manual based on paper-printed-returns) for validation; 'PPCRV was not allowed to complete when Comelec started its own canvass of senatorial and party-list candidates'; PPCRV guards 'traditional guns, goons and gold irregularities that automation could not eliminate'

Watchdog-tribute: AES Watch + Kontra Daya + Namfrel 'kept Comelec and Smartmatic on their toes... gallantly stood their ground' despite 'ballistic tantrums, dismissive attitude and threats of suits of Comelec Chair Sixto Brillantes Jr.' -- special credit for bringing PCOS-malfunction-and-18,000-of-78,000-transmission-glitches to public attention; 'nation owes them an everlasting debt of gratitude'

Reform-pursuit close: 'PCOS system had been given two electoral chances to show its worth, but it has not been flawless; has not delivered its promised 99.99 percent efficiency'; many present Comelec commissioners including Brillantes will not be on saddle in 2016; CJP trusts 'Gus Lagman, Joe Dizon and their fellow reformers will pursue the same patriotic zeal to dissect the PCOS system, and in the alternative, to help the new Comelec replace it with a better and more reliable one in light of lessons learned in the 2010 and 2013 elections'
sub_topics: Public school teachers, whom Commission on Elections always deputizes to administer polls at precinct level
Are big winners of PCOS (precinct count optical scan) automated system
No longer required to tally manually election results
They were spared from harrowing physical work, nighttime terror threats and tedious legal hassles
Under old manual system, teachers remained at polling places after voting had closed
Often into wee hours of following morning, to count manually handwritten entries on each ballot
And to enter them in 'taras' on tally boards and score sheets
Sometimes, these written entries were illegible, or appear to have been prepared by two different hands, making ballot invalid
At other times, candidates' names were written on wrong spaces, as when aspirants for mayor surfaced on spaces for vice mayor
And many times, some extraneous writings or strange drawings were scribbled on ballots, making them suspects as 'marked ballots'
These markings were used by bribers to verify votes of their 'victims'
Of course, ensuing legalistic 'objections' from lawyers confounded teachers and interminably delayed count
All these tedious difficulties were eliminated by automation
Because machines tallied ballots instantly and transmitted results electronically to municipal or city boards of canvassers
Sparing teachers not only from long horrifying process
But also from physically carrying election documents and ballot boxes from remote polling places to town centers in dead of night
(CJP is not unmindful of fact that due to transmission glitches in many -- as many as 18,000 of 78,000 -- PCOS machines
Several teachers unfortunately had to bring compact flash cards and/or machines themselves to election centers)
Because PCOS count at precinct level happened faster than speed of knowledge, old technical delays became obsolete
Teachers no longer needed to pass upon befuddling verbal skirmishes while tallying ballots at polling places
Under automated system, election returns were no longer manually prepared by teachers
Who were thus spared from signing, sealing, packing and locking them inside ballot boxes
Consequently, they could no longer be blamed and sued by nosy lawyers and desperate candidates looking for scapegoats for their defeat
They no longer need to defend themselves from false or malicious charges of bias or complicity in election frauds
Because of speedy electronic preparation of election returns, there is no more time to question their genuineness
Or authenticity of entries therein
Thus, under automated system, there are no more preproclamation controversies
Which were scourge of teachers because they were often bribed or threatened or forced to falsify election returns
Which were to be used as evidence in these preproclamation suits
Testifying during these contests is harrowing, and at very least, very demanding on teachers' time
Also big winners are Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting (PPCRV) led by Ambassador Tita de Villa
And other poll watchdogs, notably Automated Election System (AES) Watch, Kontra Daya, and National Citizens' Movement for Free Elections (Namfrel)
PPCRV conducted two parallel counts: (1) electronic and (2) manual
Manual count was based on paper election returns printed by PCOS machines at precincts prior to their electronic transmission
PPCRV collected these printed returns and used them to validate and verify electronically transmitted ones
Manual count will be final check on accuracy of automated canvass
Which by the way, PPCRV was not allowed to complete when Comelec started its own canvass of senatorial and party-list candidates
It has volunteer army of 350,000 who staffed precincts all over country
Guarding not just automation process but also traditional 'guns, goons and gold' irregularities that automation could not eliminate
AES Watch, Kontra Daya and Namfrel kept Comelec and Smartmatic on their toes
Monitoring closely entire automation process
Special credit should be accorded them for bringing to public attention PCOS malfunctions
Particularly transmission glitches in 18,000 out of 78,000 machines
Despite ballistic tantrums, dismissive attitude and threats of suits of Comelec Chair Sixto Brillantes Jr.
These watchdogs gallantly stood their ground and kept public updated on election hitches
Nation owes them everlasting debt of gratitude
It is CJP's hope, as it is hope of everyone concerned with viability of our democracy
That watchdogs continue critiquing and reviewing automation
PCOS system had been given two electoral chances to show its worth
But it has not been flawless; it has not delivered its promised 99.99 percent efficiency
Many of present election commissioners, including Brillantes, will no longer be on saddle come 2016 elections
But CJP trusts Gus Lagman, Joe Dizon and their fellow reformers will pursue same patriotic zeal to dissect PCOS system
And in alternative, to help new Comelec replace it with better and more reliable one in light of lessons learned in 2010 and 2013 elections

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban writes the fourth installment of his automated-elections quadrilogy -- three weeks after E100 (the vote-now column), two weeks after A458 (the installment-proclamation indictment), and one week after B19 (the FDI-trustworthiness column) -- turning to the human beneficiaries of PCOS automation and acknowledging the poll watchdogs who critiqued it. Public school teachers, whom the Comelec always deputizes to administer the polls at the precinct level, are the big winners of the PCOS (precinct count optical scan) automated system -- no longer required to tally manually the election results, they were spared from harrowing physical work, nighttime terror threats and tedious legal hassles. No manual tallying: under the old manual system, the teachers remained at the polling places after the voting had closed, often into the wee hours of the following morning, to count manually the handwritten entries on each ballot and to enter them in 'taras' on tally boards and score sheets; sometimes, these written entries were illegible, or appear to have been prepared by two different hands, making the ballot invalid; at other times, the candidates' names were written on the wrong spaces, as when aspirants for mayor surfaced on the spaces for vice mayor; and many times, some extraneous writings or strange drawings were scribbled on the ballots, making them suspects as 'marked ballots' -- these markings were used by bribers to verify the votes of their 'victims'; of course, the ensuing legalistic 'objections' from lawyers confounded the teachers and interminably delayed the count. All these tedious difficulties were eliminated by automation because the machines tallied the ballots instantly and transmitted the results electronically to the municipal or city boards of canvassers, sparing the teachers not only from the long horrifying process, but also from physically carrying the election documents and the ballot boxes from remote polling places to the town centers in the dead of night. (CJ is not unmindful of the fact that due to transmission glitches in many -- as many as 18,000 of the 78,000 -- PCOS machines, several teachers unfortunately had to bring the compact flash cards and/or the machines themselves to the election centers.) No legal hassles: because the PCOS count at the precinct level happened faster than the speed of knowledge, the old technical delays became obsolete -- teachers no longer needed to pass upon befuddling verbal skirmishes while tallying the ballots at the polling places; under the automated system, the election returns were no longer manually prepared by the teachers who were thus spared from signing, sealing, packing and locking them inside the ballot boxes; consequently, they could no longer be blamed and sued by nosy lawyers and desperate candidates looking for scapegoats for their defeat -- they no longer need to defend themselves from false or malicious charges of bias or complicity in election frauds. Because of the speedy electronic preparation of the election returns, there is no more time to question their genuineness, or the authenticity of the entries therein; thus, under the automated system, there are no more preproclamation controversies, which were the scourge of teachers because they were often bribed or threatened or forced to falsify election returns, which were to be used as evidence in these preproclamation suits -- testifying during these contests is harrowing, and at the very least, very demanding on the teachers' time. Other winners: also big winners are the PPCRV led by Ambassador Tita de Villa and the other poll watchdogs, notably the AES Watch, Kontra Daya, and Namfrel; PPCRV conducted two parallel counts: (1) electronic and (2) manual -- the manual count was based on the paper election returns printed by the PCOS machines at the precincts prior to their electronic transmission; PPCRV collected these printed returns and used them to validate and verify the electronically transmitted ones; the manual count will be the final check on the accuracy of the automated canvass, which by the way, PPCRV was not allowed to complete when the Comelec started its own canvass of the senatorial and party-list candidates; it has a volunteer army of 350,000 who staffed the precincts all over the country, guarding not just the automation process but also the traditional 'guns, goons and gold' irregularities that automation could not eliminate. AES Watch, Kontra Daya and Namfrel kept the Comelec and Smartmatic on their toes, monitoring closely the entire automation process; special credit should be accorded them for bringing to public attention the PCOS malfunctions, particularly the transmission glitches in 18,000 out of the 78,000 machines; despite the ballistic tantrums, dismissive attitude and threats of suits of Comelec Chair Sixto Brillantes Jr., these watchdogs gallantly stood their ground and kept the public updated on the election hitches -- the nation owes them an everlasting debt of gratitude. It is CJ's hope, as it is the hope of everyone concerned with the viability of our democracy, that the watchdogs continue critiquing and reviewing the automation -- the PCOS system had been given two electoral chances to show its worth, but it has not been flawless; it has not delivered its promised 99.99% efficiency; many of the present election commissioners, including Brillantes, will no longer be on the saddle come the 2016 elections -- but CJ trusts Gus Lagman, Joe Dizon and their fellow reformers will pursue the same patriotic zeal to dissect the PCOS system, and in the alternative, to help the new Comelec replace it with a better and more reliable one in light of lessons learned in the 2010 and 2013 elections.
